items.title: Amazon’s new 7.65GW Texas AI data center power plant could become the largest source of CO₂ pollution in the US — custom 35-turbine gas plant authorized to emit 33 million tons of annual greenhouse gases
items.description: Amazon is reportedly building a 7.65GW natural gas power plant in Texas to feed a new AI data center, with permits allowing up to 33 million tons of CO₂ emissions per year.
items.content: Copy link Facebook X Whatsapp Reddit Pinterest Flipboard Email Share this article 7 Join the conversation Follow us Add us as a preferred source on Google Newsletter Subscribe to our newsletter A new Amazon data center is set to become the single largest source of environmental pollution in the U.S., according to a New York Times report on August 8. The tech giant — which already operates the most data centers worldwide — is reportedly building a natural gas power plant in Pecos County, Texas, to power its new data center at the same site. According to project permits, the plant would generate up to 7.65 gigawatts of power using 35 natural gas turbines. The new plant — which burns natural gas to generate electricity — has been authorized to release 33 million tons of CO₂ annually, more planet-warming gases than any other power plant in the country, says the NY Times report.Conversely, Amazon had pledged to achieve net-zero carbon emissions across all its global business operations by 2040. The company made the promise in 2019 when it initiated and co-founded The Climate Pledge — a voluntary coalition of over 700 companies and partners — aimed at addressing its own corporate footprint and rallying global supply chains. However, the company has seen its emissions rise each year for the past several years, something analysts attribute to a spike in data centers to support the AI boom. The company is currently building several additional AI data centers globally, including the one that the new gas plant would power in Texas.Amazon has acknowledged the impact of its intense AI ambitions on its earlier climate pledges but insisted the company remained committed to them, despite obvious struggles. “The world looks different now than when we co-founded the climate pledge,” said Margaret Callahan, an Amazon spokeswoman. Still, “our commitment hasn’t changed,” she said, echoing similar statements by Microsoft, which is struggling to fulfill its 2030 sustainability promise amid carbon-heavy AI expansion, but insists it remains committed to it.Latest Videos FromTom's HardwareWatch full video here: As detailed in our data center power roadmap, an increasing number of hyperscalers and data center operators are switching from grid connections to dedicated on-site power generation. The “behind-the-meter” moves are being triggered mainly by the long timelines required to set up new power infrastructure to connect new power-hungry data centers to the grid, but also by growing anti-data center sentiments over irreversible hikes in the electricity bills of nearby communities.While many companies are also pursuing nuclear and renewable energy options — examples being Microsoft’s Three Mile Island nuclear deal and Meta’s agreement to secure up to 1GW of orbital solar energy capacity — gas appears to be the leading preference due to its scalability and speed of availability. The Trump administration has thrown its weight behind such projects for data centers, promoting oil, natural gas, and coal over renewable energy sources. items.author: Etiido Uko
items.titleZh: 亚马逊新得州AI数据中心发电厂装机765万千瓦，或成美国最大二氧化碳污染源——定制35台涡轮机燃气电厂获准每年排放3300万吨温室气体。
items.descriptionZh:
据纽约时报8月8日报道，亚马逊正在德克萨斯州佩科斯县建造一座新的天然气发电厂，为其同址的AI数据中心供电。根据项目许可证，该电厂将配备35台天然气涡轮机，总发电能力高达7.65吉瓦，每年获准排放3300万吨二氧化碳，使其成为美国温室气体排放量最大的单一发电设施。亚马逊目前运营着全球数量最多的数据中心，此举意味着这家科技巨头的AI基础设施将直接依赖化石燃料。

这一决策与亚马逊此前的气候承诺形成鲜明对比。2019年，亚马逊联合发起了“气候承诺”，承诺到2040年实现全球业务净零碳排放，已有700多家企业加入这一自愿联盟。然而，随着AI算力需求激增，该公司近几年的碳排放逐年攀升，此次天然气电厂的建设更是直接挑战其承诺的可行性。亚马逊发言人玛格丽特·卡拉汉承认“世界已经发生变化”，但坚称公司承诺不变，这与微软的处境相似——微软因碳密集型AI扩张正艰难履行其2030年可持续发展目标，但也坚持表示不会放弃承诺。

这一事件反映了超大规模数据中心能源获取模式的重大转变。由于从电网获取电力需要漫长的基建周期，加上周边社区对电价不可逆上涨的抵制，越来越多的运营商转向“表后”发电，即直接在数据中心园区现场发电，绕过传统电网连接。相比核能和可再生能源（如微软的三里岛核电协议、Meta的轨道太阳能项目），天然气因其可扩展性和快速部署能力成为最受欢迎的选择。特朗普政府也公开支持此类化石燃料项目，推广石油、天然气和煤炭而非清洁能源，进一步推动了这一趋势。

报道还指出，这一动向并非个例：马斯克的Colossus 2数据中心曾被曝未经许可安装59台天然气涡轮机；AI数据中心的电力需求已导致美国最大电网区域电价飙升76%。另有分析预测，到2027年，AI服务器将消耗超过传统数据中心硬件总和的电力。这些案例共同揭示了一个严峻现实：AI技术的爆发式发展正在与全球减排目标产生激烈冲突，而企业气候承诺的兑现正面临前所未有的考验。

items.title: Kansas town silences public comment on gigawatt AI data center after receiving death threats, moves to virtual meetings — shift follows physics teacher's arrest for clapping at data center hearing
items.description: Emporia, Kansas, switched to virtual city council meetings after death threats intensified against city leaders. The move also canceled public comments, prompting some members of the public to ask why it was affected, too.
items.content: Copy link Facebook X Whatsapp Reddit Pinterest Flipboard Email Share this article 1 Join the conversation Follow us Add us as a preferred source on Google Newsletter Subscribe to our newsletter The city council of Emporia, Kansas, the same council that had a teacher arrested for clapping in support of the opposition, announced that it will move its meetings online after its members received death threats. According to 404 Media, Emporia announced this move two days before the meeting set for August 5, 2026, and will also affect the one set on August 19, 2026.“In the interest of public safety, the Emporia City Commission meetings scheduled for Wednesday, August 5, 2026, and Wednesday, August 19, 2026, will be conducted virtually. No public comment period will be provided during either meeting,” the city said on its Facebook page.“The City remains committed to conducting the public’s business in an open and transparent manner while taking reasonable measures to protect the safety of elected officials, City staff, and members of the public. The City appreciates the public's understanding and cooperation as it implements these temporary measures while ensuring the continuity of City business.”Latest Videos FromTom's HardwareWatch full video here: The move to a virtual meeting is an understandable move given the death threats on some of the city leaders. However, it also canceled public comments and instead directed citizens to an email address and phone number where they can air their concerns privately. This led to some citizens airing their complaints in a protest outside the Emporia municipal auditorium.“While I don't doubt that there are credible threats, my big question is on how many there are and from where they are coming. Mayor Smith did mention in yesterday's meeting that the threats don't seem to really be coming from locals but ‘it only takes one’ to ruin a meeting so they went virtual. I feel like we're being punished for the actions of outsiders,” Lux Claridge, the person arrested in the previous council meeting, told 404 Media. You may like Teacher arrested for clapping in support of opposition at an AI data center meeting Protesters haul a guillotine to city council meeting about a potential AI data center, company rep cornered by protestors 142 AI data center protests staged in 42 states as public opposition increases “I'm not so upset about going virtual, it makes sense, but back it up with examples of these threats. I'm more upset that they opted to close public comment and I don't understand why.”One of the things that the council considered during the meeting was the petition to put a data center ban on the ballot, with the members voting unanimously to send it for judicial review. The council claimed that doing otherwise could open the city to a lawsuit from either side, although it did not elaborate on the reason why this would happen.Stay On the Cutting Edge: Get the Tom's Hardware NewsletterGet Tom's Hardware's best news and in-depth reviews, straight to your inbox.Contact me with news and offers from other Future brandsReceive email from us on behalf of our trusted partners or sponsorsWhile we haven’t heard of a local jurisdiction getting sued for passing a data center ban, one Texas senator warned a county in the state that it cannot legally impose this. So, the commissioners are likely being careful to avoid legal issues, even if they’re in another state. items.author: Jowi Morales
items.titleZh: Kansas town silences public comment on gigawatt AI data center after receiving death threats, moves to virtual meetings — shift follows physics teacher's arrest for clapping at data center hearing
items.descriptionZh:
堪萨斯州恩波利亚市（Emporia）市议会近日宣布，原定于2026年8月5日和8月19日举行的两次市委员会会议将全部转为线上进行，且不设任何公众评论环节。这一决定距离该市议会在一次涉及AI数据中心的会议上因一名教师为反对派鼓掌而将其逮捕的事件仅数周，如今市议员们因持续收到死亡威胁而被迫改变会议形式。

据404 Media报道，该市在Facebook上发布声明称，出于公共安全考虑，两次会议将以虚拟方式举行，期间不提供公众评论时段，公民只能通过电子邮件和电话私下表达关切。市府强调仍致力于“公开透明地处理公众事务”，同时采取合理措施保护民选官员、工作人员和公众的安全。然而，这一做法引发了部分市民不满，他们聚集在恩波利亚市政礼堂外举行抗议，认为取消公众评论是对全体市民的“惩罚”。

此前在该会议上因鼓掌支持反对派而被逮捕的Lux Claridge对媒体表示，他并不怀疑威胁的真实性，但质疑威胁的数量和来源。他透露，市长史密斯在会议中提到这些威胁似乎并非来自本地居民，“但只需要一个人就能搞砸会议”，所以才转为线上。Claridge感到困惑的是，市议会没有拿出具体威胁案例作为证据，却直接关闭了公众评论渠道。

会议期间，市议会还审议了一项将数据中心禁令列入选票的请愿，并一致投票决定将该提案提交司法审查。议会称，若不这样做，可能会让市政府面临来自任何一方的诉讼，但未详细说明原因。虽然目前尚未听说有地方政府因通过数据中心禁令而被起诉，但得克萨斯州一名参议员曾警告该州某县，法律上不能强行实施此类禁令。恩波利亚的委员们显然是在谨慎规避法律风险，即使他们身处另一个州。

这一事件只是全国范围内反对AI数据中心扩张浪潮的一部分。此前已有报道显示，全美42个州爆发了142起针对AI数据中心的抗议活动，公众反对情绪持续升温。恩波利亚市案更凸显了地方政府在推进AI基础设施与回应民意之间的艰难平衡，以及极端对立情绪如何直接冲击基层民主议事程序。
